\section[embarcar]{embarcar — to board; to embark}

\label{lesson:ES-C653-embarcar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the label, then the Spanish for the backpack.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: embarcar}
\textbf{embarcar} — \textquotedblleft{}to board; to embark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los pasajeros ya pueden embarcar.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Passengers can now board.}
\end{quote}

Used for planes as well as ships.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{embarcar} is built on \emph{barca} \textquotedblleft{}boat\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Late Latin \emph{barca} (EtymDB). Getting on a plane is still getting on a boat.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[el embarque]{el embarque — the boarding}

\label{lesson:ES-C653-embarque}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the backpack, then the Spanish for to board.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el embarque}
\textbf{el embarque} — \textquotedblleft{}the boarding\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El embarque empieza a las diez.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Boarding starts at ten.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La puerta de embarque} — the gate; \emph{la tarjeta de embarque} — the boarding pass.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{embarque} is built on \emph{embarcar} \textquotedblleft{}to board\textquotedblright{}, which comes from \emph{barca} \textquotedblleft{}boat\textquotedblright{}, Late Latin \emph{barca} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[el detector]{el detector — the detector; the metal detector}

\label{lesson:ES-C653-detector}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to board, then the Spanish for the boarding.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el detector}
\textbf{el detector} — \textquotedblleft{}the detector; the metal detector\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pasa por el detector sin el cinturón.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Go through the detector without your belt.}
\end{quote}

\emph{El detector de metales} — the metal detector.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{detector} came from English \emph{detector}, a word built on Latin \emph{dētegere} \textquotedblleft{}to uncover\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{tegere} \textquotedblleft{}to cover\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la bandeja]{la bandeja — the tray}

\label{lesson:ES-C653-bandeja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the boarding, then the Spanish for the detector.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la bandeja}
\textbf{la bandeja} — \textquotedblleft{}the tray\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Pon el móvil en la bandeja.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Put your phone in the tray.}
\end{quote}

At security your things go in \emph{una bandeja}; on a plane, \emph{la bandeja} is the seat tray.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bandeja} was borrowed from Portuguese \emph{bandeja} (EtymDB), which is usually linked to \emph{banda} \textquotedblleft{}side\textquotedblright{}; the details are not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la escala]{la escala — the stopover; the scale; the ladder}

\label{lesson:ES-C653-escala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the detector, then the Spanish for the tray.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la escala}
\textbf{la escala} — \textquotedblleft{}the stopover; the scale; the ladder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El vuelo hace una escala de dos horas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The flight has a two-hour stopover.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Sin escalas} — non-stop.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{escala} comes from Latin \emph{scāla} \textquotedblleft{}a flight of steps, a ladder\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{scandere} \textquotedblleft{}to climb\textquotedblright{}. The stopover sense came from sea travel, where an \emph{escala} was a port of call.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
